references.text: Jesus says that persecutions will become an opportunity to bear witness (μαρτύριον). The parallel passage in Luke 21:13 points to the same idea as in Philippians 1:12, where Paul tells us that his imprisonment has served to advance the gospel.

In Matthew 10:18 Jesus says that the disciples will be brought before governors and kings for His sake, "as a testimony to them and to the nations". This is a direct parallel to Luke 21:13 where persecution serves as a witness (εἰς μαρτύριον).
Mark 13:9 is Mark's parallel account, where Jesus says that the disciples will be brought before governors and kings for His sake, "as a testimony to them". The same expression εἰς μαρτύριον is used.

In Philippians 1:12-14 Paul describes how his chains became known throughout the whole palace guard and among all others, and that most of the brothers gained courage to preach. This concretely illustrates how persecution became a testimony, just as Jesus predicted in Luke 21:13.

In 2 Timothy 4:16-17 Paul tells us that the Lord stood by him when he appeared before the court, so that the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles hear it. Persecution became an opportunity for testimony, in line with Jesus' words in Luke 21:13.
In Acts 4:3-4 Peter and John were arrested, but many who had heard the word came to believe – the number of men was about five thousand. Thus persecution led to a powerful testimony and growth.
In Acts 8:1-4 the persecution following Stephen's martyrdom caused believers to be scattered and to preach the word everywhere. Persecution directly became a testimony, just as Jesus predicted.
